data.what: Epoch AI, ECI scores of open- and closed-weight models (chart data, open-closed gap insight)

sensitivity_confident_or_likely.what: targets and catch-up models whose compute estimate Epoch rates confident or likely

sensitivity_near_frontier.what: targets: every model with a compute estimate whose ECI is at least the standing record's lower interval end at its release; a target already matched under its own compute before its release was not at the efficient frontier and is left out of the tallies

backtest.what: Part I's design: a cap at a then-frontier model's compute (h = 0) and at h OOM below it; the first model at or below the cap to match the record's ECI. At h = 0 the expression predicts 0 for every input. Each catch-up closing more headroom than any earlier one is an event, implying a rate 10^(h / t) with J = 0

by_e1_sample.what: at the example headroom, the leak time [high jump, low jump] and the headroom needed [low jump, high jump] at each of E1's six sample rates; 'inside' means the leak time is below m * T_r at every jump in the range (the example cap fails the line), 'outside' that it exceeds it at every jump

scale_term_if_e1_full_sample_were_truste.what: the expression with E1's full-sample rate at the cap's scale (interaction fit) against one multiplier at Ho et al.'s interval, example headroom, no cheap verifier; E1's six samples do not support that rate (at or above 1e24 FLOP they give 393 and 1,512 a year), so this is not a test

c2b_fixed_compute.what: C2(b) read as: the two intervals do not overlap. Where the boundary is below the headroom needed at the low corner, every headroom at which they separate is one where the cap's leak time is below m * T_r at every input in the box. Same rate range for both, so the difference is the jump terms alone; below the boundary headroom the intervals are disjoint, above it they overlap. This is arithmetic on Part I's input ranges, not evidence that either form is right

classes.cheap_verifier: J = 0, S_v from one technique's typical saving to the cheap-verifier span
classes.no_cheap_verifier: J from the typical to the high post-training jump, S_v = 0

e1_full_sample.what: E1 on all joined models, 2.5th to 97.5th percentile of resampling

e1_subsets.what: E1's six samples of the same models, lowest to highest point

part1_bracket.what: Part I's bracket: the small-compute bound to the Rosetta rate, Ho et al. central

rosetta_families.what: the Rosetta fit across model families; its low end of 1 means no drift

corners.record_tr_note: E5's declared-path detection time plus E24's Kaplan-Meier median response; a median, not a high quantile, and a share of findings were never halted
corners.what: the exact interval of the leak time (years) at each headroom (OOM), [fast corner, slow corner], and the headroom a cap needs for the leak time to exceed m * T_r, [low, high]; by Theorem 2.1 every input in the box gives a value between the two; null means unbounded (a rate of 1)

monte_carlo.jumps: J or S_v uniform on its range

laws.log_triangular: log10 gamma triangular, peaked at the range's central value (its log midpoint when it has none)

monte_carlo.what: percentiles of the leak time inside each box, an illustration only: the box's corners are the result, and the median moves with the assumed law for the rate

other_readings.what: how the reproduced strict lag moves with two choices the page leaves open; counting blank rows as open also counts closed models (o3-pro, Gemini 3.5 Flash) as open, so it is not Epoch's reading either

open_closed_lag.what: Epoch's method with point estimates: each day, the best open-weight model so far, and the days since the last date on which the state of the art was strictly below it; the vertical gap is the state of the art minus that open model's ECI

e18-b-disjoint-example.label: of 8 pairs of class and rate range, those in which the expression's interval and a single multiplier's do not overlap at the example headroom

e18-b-sep-fails-line.label: of 8 pairs of class and rate range, those in which every headroom where the two intervals separate is one where the cap's leak time is below m * T_r at every input

e18-b-sep-part1.label: C2(b) at fixed compute, no cheap verifier, Part I's bracket for both: largest headroom at which the expression's interval and a single multiplier's do not overlap (arithmetic on the ranges)

e18-b-sep-subsets.label: the same boundary with the rate across E1's six samples

e18-b-sep-verifier-part1.label: the same boundary with a cheap verifier, Part I's bracket

e18-b-sep-verifier-subsets.label: the same boundary with a cheap verifier, rate across E1's six samples

e18-bt-censored.label: records not yet matched by any model with a compute estimate at or below their own compute when the data end

e18-bt-events.label: catch-ups below a record's compute that close more headroom than any earlier one

e18-bt-gamma-hi.label: highest yearly rate a catch-up implies, 10^(h / t) with J = 0 (upper end of the observed range)

e18-bt-gamma-lo.label: lowest yearly rate a catch-up implies, 10^(h / t) with J = 0 (lower end of the observed range, not an interval)

e18-bt-h0-hi.label: longest such time among the records that were matched

e18-bt-h0-lo.label: shortest time until a model at or below a then-frontier record's compute matched its ECI (the expression predicts 0 for every input)

e18-bt-inside-part1.label: of 7 backtest points (first matches at the record's compute and catch-ups), those inside the expression's exact interval with Part I's bracket and J = 0

e18-bt-inside-part1-j.label: of 7 backtest points, those inside the exact interval with Part I's bracket and J over Part I's post-training range

e18-bt-inside-subsets.label: of 7 backtest points, those inside the exact interval with the rate across E1's six samples and J = 0

e18-bt-max-headroom.label: largest headroom closed below a record's compute in the backtest

e18-bt-targets.label: ECI records with a compute estimate, set on or after the first closed model's ECI: the then-frontier caps the backtest can place

e18-leak-part1-hi.label: leak time of the example cap, no cheap verifier, slow corner of Part I's bracket (small-compute bound, typical jump); the exact interval's upper end

e18-leak-part1-lo.label: leak time of the example cap, no cheap verifier, fast corner of Part I's bracket (Rosetta rate, high post-training jump); the exact interval's lower end

e18-leak-subset-hi.label: leak time of the example cap at the slowest of E1's six sample rates (not open weights) and the typical post-training jump

e18-leak-subset-lo.label: leak time of the example cap at the fastest of E1's six sample rates (at or above 1e24.5 FLOP) and the high post-training jump

e18-leak-verifier-hi.label: leak time of the example cap with a cheap verifier, slow corner of Part I's bracket (span of one typical technique); the fast corner is 0, the span covering the headroom

e18-mc-median-spread.label: illustration: largest over smallest Monte Carlo median of the example cap's leak time across three assumed laws for the rate inside Part I's bracket (the median is the law's, not data's)

e18-need-part1-hi.label: headroom a cap needs for its leak time to exceed m * T_r, no cheap verifier, high corner of Part I's bracket

e18-need-part1-lo.label: headroom a cap needs for its leak time to exceed m * T_r, no cheap verifier, low corner of Part I's bracket

e18-need-record-tr-part1-hi.label: headroom needed, no cheap verifier, high corner of Part I's bracket, with T_r from the record (E5's declared-path detection plus E24's median response, not a high quantile)

e18-need-subset-hi.label: headroom a cap needs for its leak time to exceed m * T_r at the fastest of E1's six sample rates, no cheap verifier, high jump

e18-need-subset-lo.label: headroom a cap needs for its leak time to exceed m * T_r at the slowest of E1's six sample rates, no cheap verifier, typical jump

e18-need-verifier-part1-hi.label: headroom a cap needs for its leak time to exceed m * T_r, cheap verifier, high corner of Part I's bracket

e18-need-verifier-subset-hi.label: headroom a cap needs at the fastest of E1's six sample rates with a cheap verifier's full span

e18-oc-evaluable-days.label: of the window's 148 days, those on which both the best open model and the record it matched have a public compute estimate, so the expression could predict the lag

e18-oc-gap-eci.label: mean ECI gap between the state of the art and the best open model over Epoch's 2026 window, reproduced

e18-oc-lag-over-published.label: reproduced strict lag over the strict lag Epoch publishes (1 means it reproduces)

e18-oc-lag-strict.label: Epoch's open-closed lag over its 2026 window, reproduced from its chart data with point estimates (the strict version)

e18-subsets-inside-line.label: of E1's six sample rates, those at which the example cap's leak time is below m * T_r at every post-training jump in Part I's range (the cap fails the illustrative line)

e18-subsets-outside-line.label: of E1's six sample rates, those at which the example cap's leak time exceeds m * T_r at every post-training jump in Part I's range
